subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and require a narrow launch-readiness fix, or intentionally gate/serialize rapid distinct ACPX launches?
rationale: Current code and tests deliberately allow different ACP session keys to run in parallel, so changing that behavior to avoid this failure would be a compatibility/product choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve Parallelism
options.body: Run live two-spawn proof and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

options.title: Gate Rapid ACPX Launches
options.body: Intentionally serialize or throttle rapid ACPX child launches, then update tests and docs to state the reduced concurrency contract.

options.title: Wait For Fresh Repro
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info until a current ACPX/Claude repro identifies whether the old symptom still exists.

recommendation.title: Preserve Parallelism
recommendation.body: Run live two-spawn proof and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has recent ACPX runtime-surface and architecture review history, making him the best available owner for the parallelism-versus-gating decision.
